subject: Deployment-fit checklist: hosted vs dedicated vs private — HIPAA evidence gap review
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment-fit checklist: hosted vs dedicated vs private — HIPAA evidence gap review

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Thanks again for the intro call this morning — good context on your clinical extraction workload and audit cadence. Below is a short written recap and a targeted checklist so we can validate which Redwood deployment mode is the best fit (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private on-prem/VPC).

Recap (high level)
- Primary workload: document ingestion -> clinical entity extraction -> structured output to your EHR.
- PHI surface: moderate (patient identifiers in free text); peak token volume ~2.5M tokens/day, mostly daytime windows.
- Current constraint: vendor must sign a BAA; SOC2 evidence and audit access required for annual audits.
- Procurement timeline: aiming to finalize commercial terms by end of July.

Deployment tradeoffs (short)
- Hosted API: fastest to production, can work with BAA for PHI but requires clear agreement on data retention and customer-managed keys are limited vs Dedicated/Private.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs + VPC peering): predictable throughput, isolation for PHI, stronger controls around logging and KMS integration; common choice for regulated workloads that want low ops overhead.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): required when customer needs full control of key material, on-prem air-gapped deployments, or when procurement/audit requires physical access or a self-managed control plane.

Targeted evidence checklist for your team to confirm (please reply inline):
1) BAA: do you need a vendor-signed BAA before any POC data is shared? (Yes/No)
2) SOC2: do you require Redwood's Type II report? Any specific control families (CC6 logging, CC7 encryption, etc.) to emphasize?
3) KMS/HSM: must we integrate with your KMS/HSM (bring-your-own-key)? If yes, which provider (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, YubiHSM)?
4) Audit logs: what level of audit detail is required (per-request token logs, model version, user id)? How long must logs be retained?
5) Data residency: do you require EU/US-only storage or specific region?
6) SLA: required p95 latency/SLO and uptime targets for production.
7) On-prem: if Private is required, who is the internal contact for hosting and network (ops)?
8) Redlines: any must-have contract language or procurement constraints (PO terms, invoice cadence)?

Attachments: shared a draft BAA and a short SOC2 control mapping outline for your review.

Suggested mutual action plan
- This week (by Fri 11 Jul): Mediforma to confirm answers to checklist items + return security questionnaire (attached).
- Week of Jul 14: Technical readiness call (Redwood infra + Mediforma infra) to validate network and KMS options; quick demo of dedicated capacity dashboard.
- Week of Jul 21: If Dedicated looks good, run a 2-week pilot on reserved capacity (limited keys, scrubbed dataset) while legal finalizes BAA.

Next steps: can you confirm which deployment mode you prefer to evaluate first (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)? I recommend Dedicated as the primary path based on what we discussed, but happy to accommodate Private if procurement requires it.

Thanks,

Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Marcus,

Appreciate the clear recap — we filled in what we can below. Tom is on the thread for procurement and security review.

Answers to your checklist:
1) BAA: Yes, we need a fully signed BAA before any PHI-containing POC.
2) SOC2: We require your Type II report and prefer confirmation for logging (roughly equivalent to CC6) and encryption controls (CC7). We will want a short control mapping for how Redwood's controls map to our internal audit checklist.
3) KMS/HSM: Important — we need BYOK for encryption at rest. AWS KMS is our preference; we have an HSM-backed KMS for certain keys and would like to understand if Redwood supports EKMs/HSM integrations.
4) Audit logs: Need per-request tracing (request id, timestamp, model version, caller id). Retention: 1 year minimum, with the option to export longer-term.
5) Data residency: US-only for now.
6) SLA: p95 latency target ~500ms for interactive calls; uptime 99.9% desired for production.
7) On-prem: Not our preferred option; would consider for extremely sensitive pipelines, but procurement will push back on on-prem capex.
8) Redlines: standard PO/term net30, and indemnity caps tied to contract value (will need to confirm).

We've attached our security questionnaire (partly filled) — see Mediforma_security_questionnaire_filled.xlsx.

Preferred evaluation path: Dedicated capacity in a customer VPC sounds like the right first step. We want to validate KMS integration and audit log retention during the pilot.

Questions for Redwood:
- Can you confirm whether Dedicated supports attaching customer KMS keys per-customer?
- For audit logs—are those accessible via S3 buckets we control or do they live only in Redwood logs?
- If we need HSM-level key material, what is the timeline/cost to enable that?

Thanks —
Sarah

Sarah / Tom — thanks for the quick turnaround and the questionnaire. Helpful. Short answers inline and proposed next actions below.

Short answers to your questions:
- Dedicated + customer VPC: yes — Dedicated pools can be placed in customer VPCs with VPC peering/transit. Audit logs can be exported to an S3 bucket you control (we can set a cross-account sink).
- KMS/BYOK: we support AWS KMS BYOK integrations for encryption at rest and can integrate with HSM-backed KMS when keys are managed in your AWS account. For on-prem HSM appliances (YubiHSM, Thales), we have an integration path but that is a Private deployment discussion.
- HSM timeline/cost: enabling HSM-backed BYOK for Dedicated typically requires an architecture review and additional entitlements — plan ~3–4 weeks for validation and minor infra changes; there may be a one-time enablement fee depending on scale.
- SOC2: we'll share our Type II report under NDA (we typically provide this to customers during procurement). The SOC2_control_mapping_outline.docx attached has a first-pass mapping to common control families.

Proposed next steps (concrete):
1) This Friday 11 Jul: Mediforma to confirm final evaluation path (you indicated Dedicated). Please confirm the AWS account id for S3/KMS cross-account setup. (Owner: Tom / Mediforma)
2) Jul 14–16: Technical readiness call (Redwood infra + Mediforma cloud infra) — topics: VPC peering, cross-account S3, KMS BYOK flow. (Owner: Marcus + Karthik from Redwood)
3) Jul 21: Start 2-week Dedicated pilot: limited quota, mock/production routes with scrubbed dataset. Redwood to provide exportable audit logs and a short runbook for the pilot. (Owner: Marcus)
4) Legal: exchange BAA and redlines in parallel; Marcus will send a DocuSign link for the BAA draft. (Owner: Legal teams)

I've attached the SOC2 control mapping outline and the draft BAA we shared earlier. I'll also loop in Neha (cc'd) to set up the SOC2 mapping call and confirm what artifacts we can provide for the audit.

If that timeline works, I will schedule the Jul 14 readiness call and share a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Marcus
